card.name: "Of" in old Aztec history prose
card.fires_on: The word "of" (or "the" after it) right before a proper name in 19th-century narrative about Aztec and Mexican history, as in "the days of the Aztecs". Also fires on a few other words before a name.

modes.label: Of before a people or place
modes.description: "of" linking a noun like days, states, or territory to an Aztec-era name.
modes.example: On the opposite borders of the largest of these basins, much shrunk in its dimensions since the days<< of>> the Aztecs, stood the cities

modes.label: The after of
modes.description: "the" following "days of" before an empire or people.
modes.example: They were much enlarged in the latter days of<< the>> empire, when they may be considered as

modes.label: Title before a name
modes.description: A title or short verb right before a person's name.
modes.example: The Post Office Palace  <<President>> Domingo Sarmiento ordered the construction

card.plain: It marks the small linking word just before a historical name in old-style writing about the Aztecs.
